title: September 7 - 11, 2026
lede: Four sessions, and the last one decides the Fed. Labor Day is Monday Sept 7 — markets closed. August CPI lands Friday 7:30am, the final inflation print before the Sept 15-16 FOMC, with futures split roughly 50/50 between a hold and a hike. Waller has already named his condition out loud: he backs a hold unless August inflation runs hot. Apple launches the iPhone 18 Wednesday and Oracle reports Thursday. The index closed the week almost exactly where it opened it — SPY +0.11% over five sessions — while MU ran 8.8% and broke $1,000.

heroes.title: FRI 9/11 — AUGUST CPI
heroes.when: 7:30AM CT · LAST INPUT BEFORE THE FOMC
heroes.why: Headline seen holding near 3.5% y/y. This is the swing input, not payrolls — Waller said plainly he is willing to support a hold “if there is continued progress toward our 2 percent goal” but would “consider a rate hike” if inflation comes in hot, and BofA counted 61 inflation references against 30 labor references in Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. Core over the three months through July ran 3.05%, down from 4.76% in February. Watch GLD first: it is the cleanest read on whether the move is real yields or fear, and it closed Friday at 406.75, still under the 408.54 low it broke on the jobs print.

heroes.title: WED 9/9 — APPLE “SURPRISE AND SHINE”
heroes.when: TIME TBA · FIRST LAUNCH UNDER TERNUS
heroes.why: iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and a first foldable expected. The date is now confirmed. Two things make this awkward rather than clean: AAPL fell 2.50% Friday to 319.99 heading into its own event, and Nikkei reported foldable production is limited to a few hundred units a day. A launch into a falling stock with a supply constraint already public is a different setup from a launch into strength. The supplier chain is the wider expression.

heroes.title: THU 9/10 — ORCL, ADBE & PPI
heroes.why: ORCL is the September checkpoint on AI capex, with cloud growth guided north of 55%; it closed Friday +3.07% at 158.77, bid into the print. ADBE reports the same evening having just named Anil Chakravarthy as next CEO (Narayen to Executive Chair Dec 1) — the stock took that badly, −6.74% Friday to 266.50. A leadership change and a print on the same week is the rare case where guidance and credibility get priced together. August PPI lands that morning as the warm-up to Friday's CPI.

days.name: MON 9/7
days.note: Labor Day. U.S. markets closed. The China tech slate still runs and sets up Tuesday's ADR open.
econ: Labor Day — U.S. equity and bond markets closed. No releases.
events: Conference slate runs through the holiday — PDD, JD, BIDU, BABA, NTES, SE. The read lands on Tuesday's ADR open, not Monday.
A three-day weekend means Friday's book carried headline risk across it. Gaps Tuesday are as likely to be weekend news as anything domestic.

days.name: TUE 9/8
days.note: Back from the long weekend. Light on macro, and the first chance to see whether Friday's hot-print reaction held over three days.
econ: No tier-one release. The tape re-prices the CPI risk into Friday on its own.
events: Presenting. Closed the week at 356.47 after the +16.6% print reaction on 9/3 faded from +23.4% premarket.
Second conference of the run, pushed from Monday by the holiday.
Second of the two sessions after the 9/3 investor briefing — the holiday split this window across the weekend.

days.name: WED 9/9
days.note: The heaviest single-name day of the week. Apple's launch plus five reports.
econ: Quiet docket ahead of PPI Thursday and CPI Friday.
events: “Surprise and Shine” — iPhone 18 launch, first under CEO Ternus. Date confirmed, start time not published. Pro, Pro Max and a first foldable expected.
Nikkei: foldable production limited to a few hundred units per day. The constraint is public before the launch, which caps the upside surprise.
The wider expression of the event — the chain moves on unit guidance, not on the keynote.

days.name: THU 9/10
days.note: PPI in the morning, two significant reports after the close, and RBLX opens its developer conference.
econ: August PPI. The producer-side warm-up to Friday's CPI — a hot PPI moves Friday's expectations before the print lands.
events: The September AI capex read. Cloud growth guided north of 55%. Closed Friday +3.07% at 158.77.
Reports days after naming Anil Chakravarthy CEO. Closed Friday −6.74% at 266.50.
RDC26 opens, Sept 10-12, San Jose McEnery. Engine upgrades, creator tools and monetization — the supply side of bookings. Multi-day, so the move can extend. Closed Friday +4.28% at 43.29.

days.name: FRI 9/11
days.note: The week's decider. Last inflation print before the FOMC, with the market split down the middle.
econ: AUGUST CPI. Headline seen near 3.5% y/y. The single input Waller named as the thing that would flip him from a hold to a hike.
Futures roughly 50/50 on the Sept 15-16 decision. A hot print does not merely raise odds — it removes the stated condition for the hold.
events: The cleanest tell. It broke Thursday's 408.54 low on the jobs print and closed the week at 406.75, still under it. Gold falling on hot data is a real-yield move, not fear.
FOMC decision Wed 9/16. Everything this week is positioning into it.

watch.body: “Surprise and Shine” product event. Date now confirmed as Sept 9; it had previously been tracked only as a watch date. iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and a first foldable expected. Start time still unpublished. DATE CONFIRMED · TIME TBA

RDC26, Sept 10-12, San Jose McEnery Convention Center. Roblox's flagship creator gathering, where it unveils engine upgrades, creator tools and monetization — the supply side of bookings growth and the venue feeding the 10%-of-global-gaming-content ambition management repeats on calls. Multi-day, so the move can extend across the window. VERIFIED

Snapdragon Summit 2026, Sept 22-24, Maui. Qualcomm's biggest platform showcase of the year — next flagship chipset (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 expected) plus the AI, connectivity and imaging roadmap. Multi-day. VERIFIED
Q4 FY2026 earnings. Date comes from a secondary aggregator and has not been confirmed against Costco IR. Verify before trading it. UNCONFIRMED

howto: Everything before Friday is positioning, not resolution.

The FOMC is split 50/50 and CPI is the stated tiebreaker. Monday is closed, Tuesday is empty, and Wednesday and Thursday are single-name events. Nothing between now and 7:30am Friday changes the rate question — which means size taken earlier in the week is being carried into a binary, across a shortened week, whether or not that was the intent.
Watch gold, not the index, for the inflation read.

Friday's jobs print gave the template: GLD fell from 409.88 to 402.35 in three minutes while SPY moved a fifth of a percent. Gold broke Thursday's 408.54 low and never reclaimed it, closing the week at 406.75. Gold selling on hot data is a real-yield move rather than a growth scare, and it prices the Fed faster and more legibly than the index does.
Apple is a launch into weakness, which is a different trade.

AAPL fell 2.50% on Friday into its own event week, and the foldable supply constraint — a few hundred units a day, per Nikkei — is already public. Pre-announced constraints cap the upside surprise, and the reliable expression of an Apple launch has usually been the supplier chain on unit guidance rather than the keynote itself.
The index went nowhere last week; the semis did all of it.

SPY finished the week +0.11% and IWM +0.07%, while MU ran 8.8% and broke $1,000 for the first time. That divergence is the thing to respect: index-level positioning captured none of last week's actual move, and if it persists, an index hedge into CPI is not a hedge on what is actually making money.
foot: Times Central. Earnings and event dates pulled Sunday 9/6; index and single-name marks are Friday 9/4 regular-session closes from the broker, not consolidated tape. Labor Day is Monday Sept 7 — markets closed, so this is a four-session week. CPI and PPI are fixed BLS dates. Apple's event date is confirmed but no start time has been published — marked TBA, not estimated. Costco's Sept 24 date comes from a secondary aggregator and is not confirmed against company IR. Waller and Warsh quotes are from the Reuters NEXT interview of 9/3 and the Jackson Hole address respectively. Catalyst Watch is catalysts.json.
